scope: Offline export of the already-cached all-MiniLM-L6-v2 source checkpoint. This record does not claim byte parity with the historical SentenceTransformer runtime because P1's historical manifest recorded the model alias but not that package version.

historical_p1_source.observed_call_contract: SentenceTransformer.encode(texts, normalize_embeddings=True, convert_to_numpy=True, batch_size=64), then astype(float64)
historical_p1_source.pooling_contract: BERT tokenizer input truncated to 256 tokens; attention-mask mean pooling over last_hidden_state; L2 normalization; 384 dimensions

original_wrapper_oracle.environment: private CPython 3.12.13 environment, sentence-transformers 5.6.1, transformers 4.53.3, torch CPU threads=2
original_wrapper_oracle.historical_limit: The historical P1 manifest did not pin sentence-transformers; this executes the original wrapper with an explicitly pinned current local oracle, rather than proving the unrecorded historical package version.

typescript_cpu_qualification.model_loading: Transformers.js local model loading enabled; remote models disabled; private ONNX artifact only.
typescript_cpu_qualification.raw_tokenizer_counterexample: For the 300-token boundary fixture, Transformers.js 4.2.0 emitted content token 19204 in position 255 whereas the Python source tokenizer emitted terminal SEP token 102. All attention masks and token-type IDs matched.
typescript_cpu_qualification.profile_correction: After tokenizer output, preserve CLS, padding, masks, and type IDs, and replace the final visible token with configured SEP=102. This makes all four fixture input-ID rows exactly equal to the Python fixture; it reserves two special-token positions at the 256-token bound.
typescript_cpu_qualification.runtime: Node 24.13.0, @huggingface/transformers 4.2.0, bundled onnxruntime-node 1.24.3; affinity warnings from ONNX Runtime were emitted by this container but did not stop inference.

export.command: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 optimum-cli export onnx --model <cached-snapshot> --task feature-extraction --library-name transformers --dtype fp32 --device cpu --opset 17 <private-output>

cpu_qualification_fixture.qualification_platform: Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12.13, torch 2.7.1+cu126 executing CPU with two Torch threads, ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 CPU with two intra-op threads

interpretation.candidate_status: The ONNX graph is cryptographically bound to the cached safetensors source and is numerically close to a direct Transformers CPU source-checkpoint calculation on boundary-bearing tokenization cases.
not_established: Bit-exact equality: float32 source and ONNX vector byte hashes differ.
Bit-exact equality: the Node and Python float32 output byte hashes differ despite bounded residuals.
Historical SentenceTransformer package/runtime parity: its version was not pinned in the original P1 manifest.
interpretation.next_qualification: Wire the source-bound profile correction and the local-only Node backend into the Effect runtime after its package checkpoint, then retain the raw tokenizer counterexample and require fixture token equality before accepting numeric residual bounds.
